You are early_island22, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
agents form one swarm, organized into groups. You are in group_0 with brisk_harbor75, jolly_ember22, pale_kettle84, rapid_thistle87. Each agent works in
its own sandbox, on its own git repository. Your group also shares one `main` branch, which every member
can push to. Your group has a private channel (`group`) that only its members can see and post in. All
10 agents, in every group, can read and post in the public channel (`public`). Work together with
your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to coordinate within your
group, and `public` to share general findings with other groups.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Other groups cannot see your group's `main`.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is the swarm's score on this task: the highest score among all groups, where a group's score
is the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on its `main` at the end. Every agent receives the
same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents post and ask each other questions. In `group`, announce
what you are exploring, building, or have found: a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a proposal for how to organize your group's work, or a question. In `public`, share general
findings (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case) with the other groups.
- `post` publishes a message to `group` or `public`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- Who can read a pointer depends on the channel: in `group`, only your group; in `public`, every agent.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, the latest 20 posts in `public`, and any
  unopened posts that mention you, one line each (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a
  post's number shows its full text, with its pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own
  version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished in `group`, with a pointer,
  then go back to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main`
  does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve
  as many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

## Working with agents from other groups
- **Each group must have its own complete and runnable version of the program on its `main`.**
- `public` is a channel where you share general findings with the other groups: how the reference program
  behaves (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), edge cases worth testing, approaches that worked or did not, and code that
  others may find useful. Post what you learned that other groups are likely to miss. Keep the
  coordination of your own group's work in `group`.
- Read what others post in `public`. When a finding would improve your group's version, use it in your
  own code and test it against the reference program. Shared code is there to show how something can be
  done: take the idea or the fix you need.

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.
</collaboration_mode>

## Task context
Build a new implementation from scratch that matches the behavior of the reference executable.
The executable is located at `/opt/reference/executable`.
You also have access to the existing documentation.

## Your task
Implement a program whose externally observable behavior matches the reference executable.
Write it in **Python 3.10**.
- Its documentation is in `/workspace` (README and other files). There is no source code and no internet.
- Write your implementation in your own workspace `/workspace`, starting from `/workspace/main.py`.
  You may add more Python modules next to it. **Standard library only.**
- `/workspace/compile.sh` is already provided: at evaluation time it turns `main.py` into the program under
  test. **Do not run it in your workspace.** Test your code with `python3 main.py ...`.
- Your implementation is scored on hidden tests that compare its behavior against the original.

**Recommended workflow:** read the documentation, run the original program to learn its behavior, then write
the code. Start writing `main.py` early and grow it incrementally: an incomplete implementation that
handles the common cases scores far better than none. After each change, run your code against the
original to check it. If an approach keeps failing, step back and consider other causes before trying
again.

I’ll first map the CLI and bundled documentation, then probe the major input modes and implement the highest coverage behavior. I’ll also check the team channel so my work fits with what others are covering.

# Dasel Dasel (short for **Data-Select**) is a command-line tool and library for querying, modifying, and transforming data structures such as JSON, YAML, TOML, XML, CSV, and KDL. It provides a consistent, powerful syntax to traverse and update data — making it useful for developers, DevOps, and data wrangling tasks. --- ## Features * **Multi-format support**: JSON, YAML, TOML, XML, CSV, HCL, INI, KDL. * **Unified query syntax**: Access data in any format with the same selectors. * **Query & search**: Extract values, lists, or structures with intuitive syntax. * **Modify in place**: Update, insert, or delete values directly in structured files. * **Convert between formats**: Seamlessly transform data from JSON → YAML, TOML → JSON, etc. * **Script-friendly**: Simple CLI integration for shell scripts and pipelines. * **Library support**: Import and use in Go projects. --- ## Installation ### Homebrew (macOS/Linux) ```sh brew install dasel ``` ### Go Install ```sh go install github.com/tomwright/dasel/v3/cmd/dasel@master ``` ### Prebuilt Binaries Prebuilt binaries are available on the [Releases](https://github.com/TomWright/dasel/releases) page for Linux, macOS, and Windows. ### None of the above? See the [installation docs](https://daseldocs.tomwright.me/getting-started/installation) for more options. --- ## Shell Completion Dasel supports tab-completion for Bash, Zsh, Fish, and PowerShell. Generate and load the completion script for your shell: ```sh # Bash source <(dasel completion bash) # Zsh source <(dasel completion zsh) # Fish dasel completion fish | source # PowerShell dasel completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression ``` See the [shell completion docs](https://daseldocs.tomwright.me/getting-started/shell-completion) for permanent installation instructions. ## Man Page Generate and view the man page: ```sh dasel man | man -l - ``` --- ## Basic Usage ### Selecting Values By default, Dasel evaluates the final selector and prints the result. ```sh echo '{"foo": {"bar": "baz"}}' | dasel -i json 'foo.bar' # Output: "baz" ``` ### Modifying Values Update values inline: ```sh echo '{"foo": {"bar": "baz"}}' | dasel -i json 'foo.bar = "bong"' # Output: "bong" ``` Use `--root` to output the full document after modification: ```sh echo '{"foo": {"bar": "baz"}}' | dasel -i json --root 'foo.bar = "bong"' # Output: { "foo": { "bar": "bong" } } ``` Update values based on previous value: ```sh echo '[1,2,3,4,5]' | dasel -i json --root 'each($this = $this*2)' # Output: [ 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 ] ``` ### Format Conversion ```sh cat data.json | dasel -i json -o yaml ``` ### Recursive Descent (`..`) Searches all nested objects and arrays for a matching key or index. ```sh echo '{"foo": {"bar": "baz"}}' | dasel -i json '..bar' # Output: [ "baz" ] ``` ### Search (`search`) Finds all values matching a condition anywhere in the structure. ```sh echo '{"foo": {"bar": "baz"}}' | dasel -i json 'search(bar == "baz")' # Output: [ { "bar": "baz" } ] ``` --- ## Documentation Full documentation is available at [daseldocs.tomwright.me](https://daseldocs.tomwright.me). --- ## Contributing Contributions are welcome! Please see the [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for details. --- ## License MIT License. See [LICENSE](./LICENSE) for details. ## Stargazers over time [![Stargazers over time](https://starchart.cc/TomWright/dasel.svg)](https://starchart.cc/TomWright/dasel) # Selector The selector package contains everything needed to parse a selector string into an AST, which we can then execute. # Execution The execution package accepts a `model.Value`, parses a selector and executes the resulting AST on the value. # Model The model package contains the Value struct and functionality for the application. `model.Value` is just a wrapper around `reflect.Value` but provides some additional logic for easier use. +"""CSV support used by the command line implementation."""
+import csv
+import io
+
+
+def parse_csv(text, delimiter=","):
+    """Parse Dasel's header-row CSV representation into a list of maps."""
+    if not text:
+        return []
+    reader = csv.reader(io.StringIO(text, newline=""), delimiter=delimiter)
+    rows = list(reader)
+    if not rows:
+        return []
+    headers = rows[0]
+    result = []
+    for row in rows[1:]:
+        if len(row) != len(headers):
+            raise ValueError("wrong number of fields")
+        # Assignment order intentionally gives the last duplicate header precedence.
+        result.append(dict(zip(headers, row)))
+    return result
+
+
+def write_csv(value, delimiter=","):
+    """Serialize an array of maps as CSV, requiring consistent map keys."""
+    if not isinstance(value, list):
+        raise TypeError("csv writer expects root output to be a slice/array")
+    if not value:
+        return ""
+    if not isinstance(value[0], dict):
+        raise TypeError("error ranging slice: error getting map keys")
+    headers = list(value[0].keys())
+    buf = io.StringIO(newline="")
+    writer = csv.writer(buf, delimiter=delimiter, lineterminator="\n")
+    writer.writerow(headers)
+    for item in value:
+        if not isinstance(item, dict):
+            raise TypeError("error ranging slice: error getting map keys")
+        writer.writerow([_csv_scalar(item.get(key)) for key in headers])
+    return buf.getvalue()
+
+
+def _csv_scalar(value):
+    if value is None:
+        return ""
+    if isinstance(value, (dict, list)):
+        return str(value)
+    if value is True:
+        return "true"
+    if value is False:
+        return "false"
+    return str(value)

"""CSV support used by the command line implementation."""
import csv
import io


def parse_csv(text, delimiter=","):
    """Parse Dasel's header-row CSV representation into a list of maps."""
    if not text:
        return []
    reader = csv.reader(io.StringIO(text, newline=""), delimiter=delimiter)
    try:
        rows = list(reader)
    except csv.Error as exc:
        raise ValueError(str(exc)) from exc
    if not rows:
        return []
    headers = rows[0]
    result = []
    for row_no, row in enumerate(rows[1:], 2):
        # encoding/csv's reader ignores physically blank records.
        if not row:
            continue
        if len(row) != len(headers):
            raise ValueError(f"record on line {row_no}: wrong number of fields")
        # Assignment order intentionally gives the last duplicate header precedence.
        result.append(dict(zip(headers, row)))
    return result

+"""Small YAML subset for Dasel-style data conversion."""
+import json
+import re
+
+
+def _scalar(text):
+    text = text.strip()
+    if not text:
+        return ""
+    if text.startswith(('"', "'")):
+        if text.startswith('"'):
+            try:
+                return json.loads(text)
+            except Exception:
+                pass
+        if text.startswith("'") and text.endswith("'"):
+            return text[1:-1].replace("''", "'")
+    if text in ("null", "Null", "NULL", "~"): return None
+    if text in ("true", "True", "TRUE"): return True
+    if text in ("false", "False", "FALSE"): return False
+    try:
+        return json.loads(text)
+    except Exception:
+        return text
+
+
+def parse_yaml(text):
+    lines = []
+    for raw in text.splitlines():
+        if not raw.strip() or raw.lstrip().startswith("#") or raw.strip() in ("---", "..."):
+            continue
+        lines.append((len(raw) - len(raw.lstrip()), raw.strip()))
+    if not lines:
+        return None
+
+    def block(i, indent):
+        is_seq = lines[i][1].startswith("- ") or lines[i][1] == "-"
+        out = [] if is_seq else {}
+        while i < len(lines) and lines[i][0] == indent:
+            s = lines[i][1]
+            if is_seq:
+                if not (s == "-" or s.startswith("- ")): break
+                value = s[1:].strip()
+                i += 1
+                if not value:
+                    if i < len(lines) and lines[i][0] > indent:
+                        v, i = block(i, lines[i][0]); out.append(v)
+                    else: out.append(None)
+                elif ":" in value and not value.startswith(("'", '"', "[", "{")):
+                    k, rhs = value.split(":", 1); obj = {k.strip(): _scalar(rhs)}
+                    if i < len(lines) and lines[i][0] > indent:
+                        extra, i = block(i, lines[i][0])
+                        if isinstance(extra, dict): obj.update(extra)
+                    out.append(obj)
+                else: out.append(_scalar(value))
+            else:
+                if s.startswith("- ") or ":" not in s: break
+                key, rhs = s.split(":", 1); key = str(_scalar(key))
+                rhs = rhs.strip(); i += 1
+                if rhs: out[key] = _scalar(rhs)
+                elif i < len(lines) and lines[i][0] > indent:
+                    out[key], i = block(i, lines[i][0])
+                else: out[key] = None
+        return out, i
+
+    return block(0, lines[0][0])[0]
+
+
+def _ys(value):
+    if value is None: return "null"
+    if value is True: return "true"
+    if value is False: return "false"
+    if isinstance(value, str):
+        if (not value or value.strip() != value or value.lower() in ("null", "true", "false", "~")
+                or re.fullmatch(r"[-+]?(?:\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)(?:[eE][-+]?\d+)?", value)):
+            return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False)
+        return value
+    return str(value)
+
+
+def dump_yaml(value):
+    lines = []
+    def emit(v, level, prefix=""):
+        pad = " " * level
+        if isinstance(v, dict):
+            if not v:
+                lines.append(pad + prefix + "{}"); return
+            for k, child in v.items():
+                key = _ys(str(k))
+                if isinstance(child, (dict, list)) and child:
+                    lines.append(pad + prefix + key + ":")
+                    emit(child, level + 4)
+                elif isinstance(child, (dict, list)):
+                    lines.append(pad + prefix + key + (": {}" if isinstance(child, dict) else ": []"))
+                else:
+                    lines.append(pad + prefix + key + ": " + _ys(child))
+        elif isinstance(v, list):
+            if not v:
+                lines.append(pad + prefix + "[]"); return
+            for child in v:
+                if isinstance(child, (dict, list)) and child:
+                    if isinstance(child, dict) and len(child) == 1 and not isinstance(next(iter(child.values())), (dict, list)):
+                        k, val = next(iter(child.items()))
+                        lines.append(pad + prefix + "- " + _ys(str(k)) + ": " + _ys(val))
+                    else:
+                        lines.append(pad + prefix + "-")
+                        emit(child, level + 4)
+                elif isinstance(child, (dict, list)):
+                    lines.append(pad + prefix + ("- {}" if isinstance(child, dict) else "- []"))
+                else:
+                    lines.append(pad + prefix + "- " + _ys(child))
+        else:
+            lines.append(pad + prefix + _ys(v))
+    emit(value, 0)
+    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
*** End Patch";

+"""TOML output encoder for the common data model types."""
+import json
+import re
+
+
+def _key(key):
+    key = str(key)
+    return key if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]+", key) else json.dumps(key, ensure_ascii=False)
+
+
+def _val(v):
+    if v is None:
+        raise ValueError("toml encode failed: toml: cannot encode a nil interface")
+    if v is True: return "true"
+    if v is False: return "false"
+    if isinstance(v, str):
+        if "'" not in v and "\n" not in v and "\r" not in v:
+            return "'" + v + "'"
+        return json.dumps(v, ensure_ascii=False)
+    if isinstance(v, (int, float)):
+        return str(v)
+    if isinstance(v, list):
+        if any(isinstance(x, dict) for x in v):
+            return None
+        return "[" + ", ".join(_val(x) for x in v) + "]"
+    if isinstance(v, dict):
+        return None
+    raise ValueError("unsupported TOML value")
+
+
+def dump_toml(data):
+    if data is None:
+        raise ValueError("toml encode failed: toml: cannot encode a nil interface")
+    if isinstance(data, list):
+        value = _val(data)
+        if value is not None:
+            return value + "\n"
+        raise ValueError("toml encode failed: toml: cannot encode a slice")
+    if not isinstance(data, dict):
+        return _val(data) + "\n"
+    lines = []
+    def table(obj, path, array_table=False):
+        if path:
+            lines.append(("[[" if array_table else "[") + ".".join(_key(x) for x in path) + ("]]" if array_table else "]"))
+        scalars = []
+        children = []
+        arrays = []
+        for k, v in obj.items():
+            if isinstance(v, dict): children.append((k, v))
+            elif isinstance(v, list) and any(isinstance(x, dict) for x in v): arrays.append((k, v))
+            else: scalars.append((k, v))
+        for k, v in scalars:
+            value = _val(v)
+            if value is None:
+                raise ValueError("toml encode failed: toml: cannot encode a slice")
+            lines.append(f"{_key(k)} = {value}")
+        for k, v in arrays:
+            for item in v:
+                if not isinstance(item, dict):

+                if lines and lines[-1] != "": lines.append("")

+"""Basic INI reader/writer for Dasel's map-oriented representation."""
+import re
+
+
+def parse_ini(text):
+    root = {}
+    current = root
+    for raw in text.splitlines():
+        line = raw.strip()
+        if not line or line.startswith((";", "#")): continue
+        if line.startswith("[") and line.endswith("]"):
+            path = [x.strip() for x in line[1:-1].split(".")]
+            current = root
+            for key in path:
+                current = current.setdefault(key, {})
+            continue
+        if "=" not in line: continue
+        k, v = line.split("=", 1)
+        current[k.strip()] = v.strip()
+    return root
+
+
+def dump_ini(value):
+    if not isinstance(value, dict):
+        raise ValueError("ini can only represent map values")
+    lines = []
+    def section(obj, path):
+        if path:
+            if lines and lines[-1] != "": lines.append("")
+            lines.append("[" + ".".join(path) + "]")
+        for k, v in obj.items():
+            if isinstance(v, dict): continue
+            if isinstance(v, (list, tuple)):
+                raise ValueError("ini writer cannot represent slice values directly; consider using nested sections")
+            if v is None: raise ValueError("ini cannot encode nil values")
+            if isinstance(v, bool): text = str(v).lower()
+            else: text = str(v)
+            lines.append(f"{k} = {text}")
+        for k, v in obj.items():
+            if isinstance(v, dict): section(v, path + [str(k)])
+    section(value, [])
+    return "\n".join(lines) + ("\n" if lines else "")
*** End Patch";

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /workspace/kdlformat.py
+"""KDL writer for the JSON-like data model."""
+import json
+import re
+
+
+def _name(s):
+    s = str(s)
+    return s if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*", s) else json.dumps(s, ensure_ascii=False)
+
+
+def _arg(v):
+    if v is None: return ""
+    if v is True: return "#true"
+    if v is False: return "#false"
+    if isinstance(v, str): return json.dumps(v, ensure_ascii=False)
+    return str(v)
+
+
+def dump_kdl(value):
+    lines = []
+    def node(name, value, indent=0):
+        pad = " " * indent
+        if isinstance(value, dict):
+            scalar = [(k, v) for k, v in value.items() if not isinstance(v, (dict, list))]
+            children = [(k, v) for k, v in value.items() if isinstance(v, (dict, list))]
+            head = pad + _name(name)
+            for k, v in scalar:
+                head += " " + _name(k) + "=" + _arg(v)
+            if children:
+                lines.append(head + " {")
+                for k, v in children:
+                    if isinstance(v, list):
+                        for item in v:
+                            if isinstance(item, dict):
+                                node(k, item, indent + 2)
+                            elif isinstance(item, list):
+                                node(k, item, indent + 2)
+                            else:
+                                lines.append(" " * (indent + 2) + _name(k) + (" " + _arg(item) if item is not None else ""))
+                    else:
+                        node(k, v, indent + 2)
+                lines.append(pad + "}")
+            else:
+                lines.append(head)
+        elif isinstance(value, list):
+            args = "".join(" " + _arg(x) for x in value if not isinstance(x, (dict, list)) and x is not None)
+            maps = [x for x in value if isinstance(x, dict)]
+            if maps:
+                for m in maps:
+                    head = pad + _name(name)
+                    for k, v in m.items():
+                        if not isinstance(v, (dict, list)): head += " " + _name(k) + "=" + _arg(v)
+                    kids = [(k, v) for k, v in m.items() if isinstance(v, (dict, list))]
+                    if kids:
+                        lines.append(head + " {")
+                        for k, v in kids: node(k, v, indent + 2)
+                        lines.append(pad + "}")
+                    else: lines.append(head)
+            elif args:
+                lines.append(pad + _name(name) + args)
+        else:
+            lines.append(pad + _name(name) + (" " + _arg(value) if value is not None else ""))
+
+    if isinstance(value, dict):
+        for k, v in value.items():
+            if isinstance(v, list):
+                for item in v:
+                    if isinstance(item, dict): node(k, item)
+                    elif isinstance(item, list): node(k, item)
+                    else: node(k, item)
+            else: node(k, v)
+    elif isinstance(value, (list, str, int, float, bool)) or value is None:
+        node("root", value)
+    return "\n".join(lines) + ("\n" if lines else "")
*** End Patch";

+"""HCL body serializer for maps, objects, and primitive arrays."""
+import json
+
+
+def _kind(v):
+    if v is None: return "null"
+    if isinstance(v, dict): return "map"
+    if isinstance(v, list): return "array"
+    if isinstance(v, bool): return "bool"
+    if isinstance(v, int): return "int"
+    if isinstance(v, float): return "float"
+    if isinstance(v, str): return "string"
+    return type(v).__name__
+
+
+def _value(v):
+    if v is None: return "null"
+    if v is True: return "true"
+    if v is False: return "false"
+    if isinstance(v, str): return json.dumps(v, ensure_ascii=False)
+    if isinstance(v, (int, float)): return str(v)
+    if isinstance(v, list): return "[" + ", ".join(_value(x) for x in v if not isinstance(x, dict)) + "]"
+    raise ValueError("cannot encode HCL value")
+
+
+def dump_hcl(value):
+    if not isinstance(value, dict):
+        raise ValueError(f"hcl body is expected to be a map, got {_kind(value)}")
+    lines = []
+    def body(obj, level):
+        pad = " " * level
+        for k, v in obj.items():
+            if isinstance(v, dict):
+                lines.append(f"{pad}{k} {{")
+                body(v, level + 2)
+                lines.append(f"{pad}}}")
+            elif isinstance(v, list) and v and all(isinstance(x, dict) for x in v):
+                for item in v:
+                    lines.append(f"{pad}{k} {{")
+                    body(item, level + 2)
+                    lines.append(f"{pad}}}")
+            elif isinstance(v, list) and (not v or all(not isinstance(x, dict) for x in v)):
+                if v: lines.append(f"{pad}{k} = {_value(v)}")
+            else:
+                lines.append(f"{pad}{k} = {_value(v)}")
+    body(value, 0)
+    return "\n".join(lines) + ("\n" if lines else "")
*** End Patch";

'completion-powershell': 'Register-ArgumentCompleter -Native -CommandName dasel -ScriptBlock {
    param($wordToComplete, $commandAst, $cursorPosition)

    $commands = @('query', 'version', 'interactive', 'completion', 'man', 'help')
    $formats = @('csv', 'dasel', 'hcl', 'ini', 'json', 'kdl', 'toml', 'xml', 'yaml', '')
    $shells = @('bash', 'zsh', 'fish', 'powershell')

    # Find the subcommand
    $subcommand = $null
    $tokens = $commandAst.ToString().Split() | Select-Object -Skip 1
    foreach ($token in $tokens) {
        if ($commands -contains $token) {
            $subcommand = $token
            break
        }
    }

    # Get the previous word for context-sensitive completion
    $previousWord = $null
    $allTokens = $commandAst.ToString().Split()
    if ($allTokens.Count -gt 1) {
        $previousWord = $allTokens[-1]
        if ($wordToComplete -ne '') {
            if ($allTokens.Count -gt 2) {
                $previousWord = $allTokens[-2]
            }
        }
    }

    # Complete format names
    if ($previousWord -in @('--in', '--out', '-i', '-o')) {
        $formats | Where-Object { $_ -ne '' -and $_ -like "$wordToComplete*" } | ForEach-Object {
            [System.Management.Automation.CompletionResult]::new($_, $_, 'ParameterValue', $_)
        }
        return
    }

    # Complete shell names for completion command
    if ($subcommand -eq 'completion') {
        $shells | Where-Object { $_ -like "$wordToComplete*" } | ForEach-Object {
            [System.Management.Automation.CompletionResult]::new($_, $_, 'ParameterValue', $_)
        }
        return
    }

    if ($wordToComplete -like '-*') {
        $flags = @()
        switch ($subcommand) {
            $null {
                # No subcommand: global + query flags
                $flags = @('--help', '--var', '--rw-flag', '--read-flag', '--write-flag', '--in', '-i', '--out', '-o', '--root', '--compact', '--unstable', '--it', '--config', '-c', '')
            }
            'query' {
                $flags = @('--help', '--var', '--rw-flag', '--read-flag', '--write-flag', '--in', '-i', '--out', '-o', '--root', '--compact', '--unstable', '--it', '--config', '-c', '')
            }
            'version' {
                $flags = @('--help', '')
            }
            'interactive' {
                $flags = @('--help', '--var', '--rw-flag', '--read-flag', '--write-flag', '--in', '-i', '--out', '-o', '--config', '-c', '')
            }
            'completion' {
                $flags = @('--help', '')
            }
            'man' {
                $flags = @('--help', '')
            }
            
        }
        $flags | Where-Object { $_ -ne '' -and $_ -like "$wordToComplete*" } | ForEach-Object {
            [System.Management.Automation.CompletionResult]::new($_, $_, 'ParameterName', $_)
        }
        return
    }

    # Complete subcommands
    if (-not $subcommand) {
        $commands | Where-Object { $_ -like "$wordToComplete*" } | ForEach-Object {
            [System.Management.Automation.CompletionResult]::new($_, $_, 'Command', $_)
        }
    }
}

.SH NAME
dasel \- Query and modify data structures from the command line.
.SH SYNOPSIS
.B dasel
[\fIflags\fR]
[\fIquery\fR]
.br
.B dasel
\fIcommand\fR
[\fIflags\fR]
.SH DESCRIPTION
.B dasel
is a command-line tool for querying and modifying data structures.
It supports multiple data formats including JSON, YAML, TOML, CSV, XML, and KDL.
.SH COMMANDS
.TP
.B query
[default] Execute a query
.TP
.B version
Print the version
.TP
.B interactive
Start an interactive session (alpha)
.TP
.B completion
Generate shell completion script
.TP
.B man
Generate man page

.SH OPTIONS
The following options are available for the default \fBquery\fR command:
.TP
\fB\-\-var\fR
Variables to pass to the query. E.g. --var foo="bar" --var baz=json:file:./some/file.json
.TP
\fB\-\-rw-flag\fR
Read/Write flag to customise parsing/output. Applies to read + write E.g. --rw-flag csv-delimiter=;
.TP
\fB\-\-read-flag\fR
Reader flag to customise parsing. E.g. --read-flag xml-mode=structured
.TP
\fB\-\-write-flag\fR
Writer flag to customise output. E.g. --write-flag csv-delimiter=;
.TP
\fB\-i\fR, \fB\-\-in\fR
The format of the input data.
.TP
\fB\-o\fR, \fB\-\-out\fR
The format of the output data.
.TP
\fB\-\-root\fR
Return the root value.
.TP
\fB\-\-compact\fR
Output in compact mode (no indentation/newlines).
.TP
\fB\-\-unstable\fR
Allow access to potentially unstable features.
.TP
\fB\-\-it\fR
Run in interactive mode (alpha).
.TP
\fB\-c\fR, \fB\-\-config\fR
Path to config file

.SH GLOBAL OPTIONS
.TP
\fB\-h\fR, \fB\-\-help\fR
Show context-sensitive help.

.SH QUERY OPTIONS
.TP
\fB\-\-var\fR
Variables to pass to the query. E.g. --var foo="bar" --var baz=json:file:./some/file.json
.TP
\fB\-\-rw-flag\fR
Read/Write flag to customise parsing/output. Applies to read + write E.g. --rw-flag csv-delimiter=;
.TP
\fB\-\-read-flag\fR
Reader flag to customise parsing. E.g. --read-flag xml-mode=structured
.TP
\fB\-\-write-flag\fR
Writer flag to customise output. E.g. --write-flag csv-delimiter=;
.TP
\fB\-i\fR, \fB\-\-in\fR
The format of the input data.
.TP
\fB\-o\fR, \fB\-\-out\fR
The format of the output data.
.TP
\fB\-\-root\fR
Return the root value.
.TP
\fB\-\-compact\fR
Output in compact mode (no indentation/newlines).
.TP
\fB\-\-unstable\fR
Allow access to potentially unstable features.
.TP
\fB\-\-it\fR
Run in interactive mode (alpha).
.TP
\fB\-c\fR, \fB\-\-config\fR
Path to config file

.SH INTERACTIVE OPTIONS
.TP
\fB\-\-var\fR
Variables to pass to the query. E.g. --var foo="bar" --var baz=json:file:./some/file.json
.TP
\fB\-\-rw-flag\fR
Read/Write flag to customise parsing/output. Applies to read + write E.g. --rw-flag csv-delimiter=;
.TP
\fB\-\-read-flag\fR
Reader flag to customise parsing. E.g. --read-flag xml-mode=structured
.TP
\fB\-\-write-flag\fR
Writer flag to customise output. E.g. --write-flag csv-delimiter=;
.TP
\fB\-i\fR, \fB\-\-in\fR
The format of the input data.
.TP
\fB\-o\fR, \fB\-\-out\fR
The format of the output data.
.TP
\fB\-c\fR, \fB\-\-config\fR
Path to config file

.SH EXAMPLES
.TP
Query JSON from stdin:
echo '{"name": "Tom"}' | dasel 'name'
.TP
Convert JSON to YAML:
echo '{"name": "Tom"}' | dasel -i json -o yaml
.TP
Query with compact output:
echo '{"name": "Tom"}' | dasel -i json -o json --compact
.SH SEE ALSO
.UR https://daseldocs.tomwright.me
Dasel documentation
